newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian observers to watch Pakistan elections.
newsitem.headline: Indian observers to watch Pakistan elections.

text.p: India will send a 10-member team to Pakistan as part of a South Asian delegation of observers to watch national elections in Pakistan next week, Indian officials said on Wednesday.
The decision follows an agreement by the seven-nation South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC), which includes India and Pakistan, to send poll observers to member countries.
The officials said the visit by an Indian delegation to Pakistan was approved by New Delhi despite fears by Indian diplomats that it could set a precedent.
"It is easy to predict Pakistan demanding a visit to Kashmir when we hold polls there," a foreign ministry official told Reuters. "What do we do then?"
India and Pakistan have not held official talks for three years. The two countries have fought two of their three wars over Kashmir since independence from Britain in 1947.
Other members of the SAARC team to watch Pakistani polls from January 29 will come from Nepal, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka, the officials said.
